title: Protests against Pashinyan begin in Armenia after the Karabakh ceasefire
body:
Protests began in Armenia on 10 November 2020, after Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan signed the Nagorno-Karabakh ceasefire statement that ended six weeks of fighting. Many Armenians viewed the deal as a defeat and protesters called Pashinyan a traitor. Their demands included his resignation and a one-year interim national unity government followed by snap elections. Two opposition coalitions led the movement: the pro-Western National Democratic Pole and the pro-Russian Homeland Salvation Movement, which included the Republican Party, Prosperous Armenia and the Armenian Revolutionary Federation.

On 3 December 2020 the Homeland Salvation Movement named former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan as its candidate to lead an interim government. About 15,000 people rallied outside parliament on 9 December, when Pashinyan said he would resign only if the people demanded it. A general strike on 22 December revived the protests and the opposition set up tents in Republic Square.

On 25 February 2021 the Chief of the General Staff, Onik Gasparyan, and more than 40 senior officers called for Pashinyan's resignation, which he denounced as an attempted coup. On 18 March 2021 Pashinyan announced early parliamentary elections for 20 June 2021 and said he would resign in April while remaining interim prime minister until the vote. He was re-elected in those elections. More than 362 people were reported detained during the protests, which are dated from 10 November 2020 to 25 April 2021.
